papers.title: Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. Yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. The joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. Here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact detector likelihood determines the posterior. For a simulated one-year LISA-Taiji observation, within one ring sector we obtain, for the first time, a 14-parameter posterior of a spinning EMRI from the complete prior, the most precise yet obtained for such a source from broad priors. The redshifted mass and spin of the massive black hole are determined to two parts in $10^5$, the mass two orders of magnitude beyond any electromagnetic measurement. The compact object's redshifted mass is measured to one part in $10^4$, and its eccentric, retrograde orbit discriminates between capture channels. The 0.8% distance and sub-square-degree localization are sufficient for dark-siren cosmology. Year-long coherent analysis resolves the inspiral driven by radiation reaction itself.

papers.title: Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. No compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. In particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the Nariai--Bertotti--Robinson system. For compact systems with connected horizon, the electric field vanishes even when the system is not simply connected, and the area of the horizon is either $12\pi/\Lambda$, for de Sitter, or at most $4\pi/\Lambda$. With several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged Nariai systems; its charged Hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the Reissner--Nordstr\"om--de Sitter black holes. Compact systems with horizons are spherical space forms with balls removed. Noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $\pi_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.

papers.title: DEC Fill-ins, the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, and positive mass theorems with untrapped boundary
papers.abstract: Given a closed $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold equipped with prescribed spacetime Bartnik data, we ask when this can be realised as the boundary of a compact $n$-dimensional initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition (DEC). This is a natural generalisation of the problem of non-negative scalar curvature fill-ins, where the boundary metric and mean curvature are prescribed. We give conditions on the Bartnik data that suffice to prove the existence of such DEC fill-ins with inner MOTS boundary, and give some applications of these fill-ins. Our first application of these is a lower bound on the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, which we slightly reformulate here to be a genuine spacetime definition. Our other applications include proving a positive mass theorem for spin initial data with boundary that need not be trapped, and a spacetime Penrose-like inequality that gives a positive lower bound on the mass of an initial data set with boundary in terms of its boundary Bartnik data assuming the spacetime Penrose inequality holds.

papers.title: Free hyperboloidal evolution in 3D: gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Hyperboloidal evolution allows to reach future null infinity within numerical relativity simulations. This work extends the conformal compactification approach with BSSN/Z4 from spherical symmetry to full 3D simulations. This is the first free numerical hyperboloidal evolution in 3D with a common formulation of general relativity. In this first step, gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves perturbing Minkowski spacetime are evolved nonlinearly and show that the implementation is reliable and signals can be successfully extracted at future null infinity.

papers.title: The Schwarzschild-Kerr crossover of high overtone quasinormal modes
papers.abstract: A slowly rotating black hole is close to a nonrotating one, but its highly damped quasinormal spectrum is not. The Schwarzschild approximation holds only up to overtone numbers of order $\chi^{-4/3}$, where $\chi$ is the dimensionless spin. We find that the frequency shift at this scale is a universal function, derived from the wave boundary conditions with an error estimate. It is given by the spectrum of a sextic oscillator, via the correspondence between ordinary differential equations and integrable models. It recovers the Schwarzschild $\log 3$ and organizes the singular Kerr coefficients.

papers.title: Horizon dynamical entropies and phase space topology
papers.abstract: We study phase space topologies induced by infinite-dimensional norms as a means to solve the problem of 'integrability' of Hamiltonian generators corresponding to diffeomorphisms of a null hypersurface, with the specific goal in mind to compare different prescriptions for the dynamical entropy of black holes, which replaces the area in non-stationary regimes. We first show that for a scalar field, there exists a family of norms that would provide integrability for different polarizations. We then show that a single member of this family applies to the gravitational field, and it is given by the Sobolev norm already considered in the literature. The obstruction to the other candidates lies in the semi-positivity of the metric.

papers.title: Exact general solutions for cosmological scalar field evolution in a vacuum-energy dominated expansion
papers.abstract: We derive exact general solutions (as opposed to attractor particular solutions) for the evolution of a scalar field $\phi$ in a universe dominated by a background fluid with equation of state parameter $w_B = -1$, extending earlier work on exact solutions with $w_B > -1$. Straightfoward exact solutions exist when the evolution is described by a linear differential equation, corresponding to constant, linear, and quadratic potentials. In the nonlinear case, exact solutions are derived for $V = V_0\ln \phi$, $V = V_0 \phi^{1/2}$ and $V = V_0/\phi$, and the logarithmic potential also yields an exact first integral. These complicated parametric solutions are considerably less useful than those derived previously for a universe dominated by a barotropic fluid such as matter or radiation with $w_B > -1$. However, we generalize the slow-roll approximation and show that it applies to all sufficiently flat potentials in the case of a vacuum-dominated expansion, while it never applies when the universe is dominated by a background fluid with $w_B > -1$.

papers.title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
papers.abstract: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalise the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including general axial conditions that allow for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behaviour of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.

papers.title: Late-time cosmic acceleration from matter inhomogeneities: constraints from DESI DR2 and SNe Ia
papers.abstract: We present the first observational constraints on the Misner-Sharp (MS) mass of the universe, within a newly proposed exact General Relativity solution providing a non-perturbative description of nonlinear cosmic structure formation. At early times, when statistical homogeneity and isotropy are satisfied, our model reduces to usual FLRW cosmology, accommodating Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data. At late times, the departure from homogeneity and isotropy on scales $\lesssim 200$ Mpc -- codified in the scale-dependent redshift distribution of the MS mass -- naturally induces cosmic acceleration, through an extensive term generated by the MS mass asymptotic limit on large scales. We derive the MS mass from Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and Type Ia Supernovae, obtaining a value of the cosmological constant in agreement with $\Lambda$CDM results. We outline broader implications and future observational prospects, highlighting how multi-probe strategies -- particularly CMB lensing and the late Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect -- can ultimately test this solution to the dark energy puzzle.

papers.title: Multiscale Zoom-in Lattice Simulation for Inflation
papers.abstract: Lattice simulations are a powerful tool for studying the nonlinear evolution of inflationary fluctuations. The exponential expansion, however, makes it challenging to cover a broad range of scales relevant for the dynamics, limiting how many e-folds a single fixed grid can follow. We develop a three-dimensional zoom-in lattice method to follow inflationary fluctuations over a broad range of scales from the adiabatic subhorizon regime through horizon crossing. Every few e-folds, the grid is refined into one or more subgrids, with small-scale power injected and large-scale fluctuations inherited from previous generations. Each zoom shifts the resolved band while keeping its dynamic range fixed. This extends the duration over which lattice simulations can follow inflationary fluctuations from a few e-folds to tens of e-folds. In a Starobinsky benchmark evolved for 50 e-folds, the curvature power spectrum agrees with linear theory. In a model with an oscillatory feature, the zoom-in simulations recover the peak seen in a high-resolution fixed-grid run and show scale-dependent non-Gaussianity.

papers.title: Inflation at strong mixing as a connection problem: effective field theory, Stokes phenomenon and the cosmological collider
papers.abstract: We study a massive field strongly mixed with the curvature perturbation during inflation, in the regime where the latter is described at low energies by a single-field effective field theory (EFT) with a quadratic dispersion relation. What this EFT captures, and what lies beyond it, are encoded in a connection problem, which relates the solutions that define the vacuum at early times to those that describe observables at late times. We solve it with a general method that does not rely on an exact solution. An expansion in the inverse mixing, keeping both fields, yields the EFT as its leading order, with corrections under systematic control. It selects the vacuum of the EFT, fixes a phase that the EFT cannot determine on its own, and describes the heavy mode at all times. Particle production lies beyond all orders of this asymptotic expansion. We show that it arises from a Stokes phenomenon at the complex branch points of the dispersion relation and that, in a rotating basis of the two fields, it reduces to the familiar production of particles with half the heavy mass. A reflection symmetry of the equations of motion, combined with the canonical commutation relations, then determines all exponentially small effects exactly, and with them the solution of the connection problem, which combines particle production with a conversion between light and heavy quanta. Together with the expansion, these exact results give a compact analytical formula for the cosmological collider signal, whose exponential suppression, half of the usual Boltzmann one, directly reflects the halved mass of the produced particles. The expansion only requires a separation of scales and the adiabaticity of the heavy mode, while the reflection symmetry holds for many systems in de Sitter space. We therefore expect this approach to bring physical understanding and simple formulas well beyond the present case.

papers.title: A Gauge Pathway to an Ultralight Axion through a Hidden Portal
papers.abstract: We study a gauge realization of an ultralight axion with a hidden $SU(2)$ interaction, an Abelian vector portal, a charged Higgs and a St\"uckelberg field. The vector absorbs one scalar combination and leaves a physical phase. Its normalization is fixed by the Higgs and St\"uckelberg scales, while hidden confinement generates its mass. Keeping this phase ultralight requires an additional symmetry: the displayed gauge charges alone allow large phase-dependent scalar interactions. We quantify the suppression required of these interactions. Pure-$SU(2)$ lattice results relate the susceptibility to physical confinement scales; one- and two-loop running illustrate the dependence on the chosen high-energy coupling. We derive the coherent radiation-era density and exhibit an initial angle giving the reference dark-matter abundance for $F_\chi\simeq10^{17}\,\GeV$ and zero-temperature mass $m_{\chi,0}=3\times10^{-20}\,\eV$. We follow the confined population through number-changing and number-conserving limits and bound its energy contribution. An illustrative inflaton background satisfies the stated vacuum and isocurvature tests, conditional on control of a large portal correction to its potential. Its cold hidden history requires a hidden-to-visible reheating fraction near $5\times10^{-12}$, whose microscopic origin remains an input. A second, gauge-anomaly-free model gives the same physical phase scale using two charged Higgs singlets. These constructions specify conditional cosmological examples and the additional protection and reheating mechanisms needed to complete them.

papers.title: Magnetic Catalysis and Fermion Mass Generation in de Sitter Spacetime
papers.abstract: We consider the dynamics of a charged fermion in de Sitter space in the presence of a uniform background magnetic field, and discuss magnetic catalysis of chiral symmetry breaking using the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model. We evaluate the mode functions of the charged fermion field in this background by imposing the Bunch--Davies vacuum condition. The gap equation is solved in the mean-field approximation. We derive analytic expressions for the gap in several limiting regimes, such as the large-magnetic-field and large-curvature limits. We find that the curvature effect restores chiral symmetry, whereas the magnetic field enhances chiral symmetry breaking through the conventional mechanism of magnetic catalysis. The phase structure associated with chiral symmetry breaking is revealed by numerical calculations.

papers.title: Tidally Induced Coda: Double Transients from Black Hole-Star Binary Encounters with Massive Black Holes
papers.abstract: Dense stellar environments surrounding massive black holes (MBHs) provide a natural setting for dynamical interactions that can produce transient electromagnetic and gravitational-wave sources. In particular, the tidal field of an MBH can strongly perturb binaries undergoing close encounters with it, driving their internal orbits to extreme eccentricities. Here, we investigate the outcomes of such interactions for binaries composed of a stellar-mass black hole (BH) and a star. Using direct few-body scattering experiments with the code SpaceHub, we explore hyperbolic encounters between BH-star binaries and MBHs. We systematically quantify the probabilities of different dynamical outcomes as functions of the binary orbital parameters and MBH mass, with particular emphasis on a channel in which the tidally induced eccentricity triggers a micro-tidal disruption event ($\mu$TDE), as the star is disrupted by its BH companion, followed by accretion of the stellar debris onto the MBH. We derive fitting formulae for the $\mu$TDE cross section and for the time delay between the two resulting flares, finding that the latter can be a few months for an MBH of $10^6\,M_\odot$. These double transients offer a distinctive observational signature of $\mu$TDEs. We estimate event rates ranging from a few to $\sim 100\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ within a luminosity distance of $40\,{\rm Gpc}$.

papers.title: A source-based decomposition of thermal noise for mechanical system design
papers.abstract: Thermal noise limits the sensitivity of precision mechanical instruments. We present a thermal- noise formulation for lumped-element mechanical systems that writes the total displacement thermal noise at the readout as the sum of contributions from all dissipative elements. For each contribution, we separate the thermal force generated by the element from its transfer to the readout. This decomposition provides simple design rules for comparing contributions from elements in series and in parallel and identifying the dominant noise source. It applies to frequency-dependent dissipation and to elements at different steady temperatures under local thermal equilibrium. We use it to identify the frequency regimes in which parallel and series dissipation dilution reduce displacement thermal noise. We then use examples of a pendulum on a lossy support, a rotational flexure, and rigidly mounted lunar optics to show how support noise can dominate even when the support has little effect on the system dynamics. Finally, a feedback-controlled suspension illustrates how sensing and actuation noise can be included in the same displacement-noise budget.

papers.title: $\Phi$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
papers.abstract: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present $\Phi$asmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $\Phi$-Stages, each augmented by a $\Phi$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $\Phi$-Feedback. Applied to the 11-dimensional parameters of precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals (IMRPhenomXPHM), it predicts phase-averaged optimal SNR for a single detector at fixed Advanced LIGO design sensitivity. With approximately 732k parameters, it outperforms MLP, 1D-ResNet and Transformer-encoder baselines under matched training across $10^5$--$10^6$ samples. At $10^6$ samples, it achieves $100-\mathrm{MAPE}=98.73\%$ on the held-out test set, $99.29\%$ after rank-preserving monotonic (PCHIP) calibration, and $99.39\%$ ($R^2=0.9998$) in the detection-relevant regime $\rho>8$, with stable accuracy across independent dataset realizations. On a single GPU, it sustains approximately $1.2\times10^5$ SNR evaluations per second and processes a $10^6$-injection catalogue end-to-end in approximately 8.3 s, about two orders of magnitude faster than conventional waveform-and-inner-product calculations on a 16-core CPU. Exact distance rescaling through $\rho\propto1/d_L$ supports repeated catalogue-wide detectability evaluations. The fully documented pipeline is intended as a reproducible benchmark, while results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications. Although demonstrated for a fixed single-detector configuration, the construction supports extensions to detector networks and epoch-specific sensitivities. (Abridged)

papers.title: Longitudinal-dither wavefront sensing: Calibration-free measurement of mode mismatch
papers.abstract: Mode mismatch between a gravitational-wave detector and the beams injected into it lowers the power stored in the arms and the level of squeezing. Correcting it requires the complex amplitudes of the three second-order modes, measured on a calibrated scale with the cavity on resonance at its operating power. Here we present a method that obtains a signal proportional to the mismatch by moving the beam on the wavefront sensors already used for alignment control. A longitudinal dither of the cavity adds to the resonant mode a reference field, which reaches the sensors through the same signal chains and so calibrates both the scale of this signal and the Gouy phases of the sensors and actuators, with no external calibration. We demonstrate the method on an optical cavity held on resonance in its operating state at input powers of 2 W and 62 W. At 2 W it yields an optical model that agrees with independent measurements in the mode content, and with the layout model in the actuator Gouy phase within its uncertainty of about $1^\circ$. At 62 W the thermally induced change of the eigenmode is decomposed into waist-size and waist-position changes. The method requires only components that every controlled cavity already possesses and enables continuous in situ monitoring of the mode matching in the operating state.

papers.title: On the evidence of lensing in GW231123
papers.abstract: Just like light, gravitational waves may be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their travel path, however, this has not been observed so far. GW231123 is the most massive binary black-hole merger observed to-date, and quasi-circular gravitational wave analyses infer high masses and spin parameters that are particularly sensitive to the waveform model used. Here we investigate whether gravitational lensing can account for these features. We model the signal as a superposition of multiple overlapping images of the same merger and find support for lensing across four waveform models. The lensing interpretation reduces the support for these high spins, bringing both the inferred spins and masses into closer agreement across waveform models. A comparison with a background of unlensed signals gives the lensing interpretation an estimated significance of $3.96^{+0.68}_{-0.30}\sigma$. This makes lensing a compelling interpretation of this event but is insufficient for a definitive claim.

papers.title: Analytic response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of TDI combinations
papers.abstract: Ultralight scalar fields are important candidates for dark matter. As coherently oscillating fields, they can leave characteristic signatures in space-based gravitational-wave detectors through their coupling to test masses. In this paper, we derive analytic expressions for the response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of time-delay interferometry (TDI) combinations. Starting from the coupling action between the scalar field and a test mass, we obtain the additional displacement of the test mass and the single-link Doppler response. We then give the general analytic form of the response function for an arbitrary TDI combination and compare the analytic and Monte Carlo numerical results for the optimal combinations A, E, and T. Finally, we analyze the responses of multiple types of TDI combinations, classify them into ordinary and {\zeta} types according to their low-frequency behavior, and give the low-frequency response expressions of the individual combinations. The results can be used to evaluate the sensitivity of space-based gravitational-wave missions such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin to the mass and coupling parameters of ultralight scalar-field dark matter.

papers.title: Investigating tidal heating in neutron stars via gravitational Raman scattering
papers.abstract: We present a scattering amplitude formalism to study the tidal heating effects of nonspinning neutron stars incorporating both worldline effective field theory and relativistic stellar perturbation theory. In neutron stars, tidal heating arises from fluid viscosity due to various scattering processes in the interior. It also serves as a channel for the exchange of energy and angular momentum between the neutron star and its environment. In the interior of the neutron star, we first derive two master perturbation equations that capture fluid perturbations accurate to linear order in frequency. Remarkably, these equations receive no contribution from bulk viscosity due to a peculiar adiabatic incompressibility which arises in stellar fluid for non-barotropic perturbations. In the exterior, the metric perturbations reduce to the Regge-Wheeler (RW) equation which we solve using the analytical Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi (MST) method. We compute the amplitude for gravitational waves scattering off a neutron star, also known as gravitational Raman scattering. From the amplitude, we obtain expressions for the electric quadrupolar static Love number and the leading dissipation number to all orders in compactness. We then compute the leading dissipation number for various realistic equation-of-state(s) and estimate the change in the number of gravitational wave cycles due to tidal heating during inspiral in the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) band. We find that the shear-viscous contribution is small. Even for cold ($T\sim 10^5$K) and weakly compact stars it changes the number of cycles by less than $10^{-2}$, about an order of magnitude below the other conservative 4PN contributions, and it decreases as $T^{-2}$ for hotter stars.

papers.title: Spiral Density Waves and Torque Balance in the Kerr Geometry
papers.abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) in relativistic accretion discs are a key science target for the upcoming LISA mission. Existing models of disc-EMRI interactions typically rely on crude dynamical friction or Newtonian planetary migration prescriptions, which fail to capture the relativistic fluid response induced by the binary potential. In this work we address this gap by providing the relativistic calculation. We apply standard methods from self-force theory, black hole perturbation theory, and relativistic stellar perturbation theory to compute the relativistic analogue of the spiral density wave and torque-balance results underlying planetary migration. Specifically, we calculate the response of a perfect fluid disc to the perturbing potential of an EMRI, consistently incorporating pressure effects. Using a master enthalpy-like variable and linearised fluid theory, we present a set of proof-of-principle calculations that reconstruct the fluid perturbations and relativistic spiral arm structure for a range of spin values in the Kerr geometry. We derive a relativistic torque-balance equation that enables us to compute and compare local torques with the angular momentum advected through the disc, finding striking agreement when applied to our relativistic disc-EMRI solutions. This opens a promising route towards establishing torque-balance relations between integrated disc torques arising from fluid perturbations and the forces acting on EMRIs embedded in matter.

papers.title: Statistics of time and frequency-averaged spectra in gravitational-wave background searches
papers.abstract: Time series analysis from gravitational-wave detectors often relies on the assumption that time chunks, or frequency bins, are uncorrelated. We discuss the validity of this approximation in the context of searches for stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds. We examine the impact of averaging over time and frequency, a reduction technique commonly employed to minimize the computational expense of likelihood evaluations. We introduce an analytical tool based on Fisher information to quantify the error in parameter inference arising from ignoring these effects. Finally, we address the issue of locally stationary processes and optimal time chunking. As an application, we study examples based on simulated data of the LISA space mission.

papers.title: Shadow and Polarized Images of Schwarzschild-MOG Black Hole Illuminated by Thick Accretion Disk
papers.abstract: Recent EHT polarimetric observations provide a powerful probe of near-horizon physics and modified gravity. We investigate the shadow and polarization images of a static Schwarzschild-MOG black hole illuminated by geometrically thick, optically thin accretion flows. Adopting a phenomenological model and the Hou disk model, and solving null geodesics and relativistic radiative transfer, we study how the MOG parameter, inclination angle, anisotropic synchrotron emission, and flow geometry affect the total intensity and linear polarization. It is found that the MOG parameter mainly enlarges and brightens higher-order photon rings and broadens the shadow, while the inclination angle breaks axial symmetry and enhances polarized emission inside the shadow. The Hou disk model suppresses off-equatorial radiative interference and localizes polarization signals within higher-order rings. Electric vector position angle (EVPA) patterns are mostly azimuthal but vary rapidly near lensed images. These results provide theoretical diagnostics for constraining MOG with EHT/ngEHT polarimetric observations.

papers.title: The Hidden Simplicity of the Classical Limit
papers.abstract: We study the classical limit of two-to-two massive-scalar amplitudes at all orders of perturbation theory. We compute these amplitudes in the probe limit for several theories: a family of scalar theories, electrodynamics, and $\mathcal{N}=8$ supergravity with half-BPS matter. We show that related multiple-emission classical amplitudes obey a simple factorization derivable from the usual factorization of quantum amplitudes. The classical factorization, which reflects the second-order nature of classical dynamics, holds in more general theories --- including gravity. We further show that both the multiple-emission and the two-to-two classical amplitudes have a simple organization in terms of weighted trees. This allows a recursive computation to all orders in the probe limit. The probe's trajectory emerges as a generating function of trees. The required boundary conditions are given by the Feynman $i \varepsilon$ prescription, leading to a novel worldline Green's function. In our approach, the rich classical dynamics arises from simple combinatorics.

papers.title: A Kerr-black-hole worldline action to $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$
papers.abstract: We establish a worldline action which correctly reproduces Kerr-black-hole dynamics up to fifth order in Newton's constant in a physical post-Minkowskian counting. This encompasses operators up to second order in the Riemann curvature tensor and up to fourth order in the spin tensor. Doing so entails performing the full effective-field-theory computation of the amplitude for a gravitational-wave scattering off of a spinning compact object up to four-loop order, and matching the result to the predictions from linear black hole perturbation theory. Quadratic-in-curvature operators which must be added to match successfully include time-reversal anti-symmetric ones at linear and cubic spin orders, capturing absorption across the black hole horizon, and conservative quadratic-in-spin ones. As an immediate application of our action, we compute the leading-order change in spin magnitude, and reproduce the leading change in mass, for a Kerr black hole in a scattering event with a second compact body, considering a generic orientation of the black hole's spin.

papers.title: How to Play a Black Hole: Understanding Quasinormal Mode Excitation
papers.abstract: Understanding the excitation of black hole quasinormal modes is essential for interpreting gravitational-wave signals and inferring black hole properties from them. In this work, we investigate the excitation of the quasinormal modes of Schwarzschild black holes under controlled probes. In the absence of a source, we find that broader initial data suppresses mode excitation, enhancing the relative contribution of the late-time tail, while data localized near the light ring strongly suppresses overtones relative to the fundamental mode. On the other hand, plunging sources give rise to two distinct ringdown stages, associated with scattered radiation generated during the particle's infall and with the particle crossing the light ring. Finally, we investigate how much of the signal is sourced from the strong-field region by switching off the source at some finite radius. The resulting waveform is exponentially close -- in cutoff radius -- to that of a standard infall. These results provide insight into the dependence of QNM excitation on the properties and dynamics of the perturbation, and offer a controlled setting in which to investigate the origin of black hole ringdown.

papers.title: Refined R\'enyi Entropy from Replica-Geometry Tensor Networks
papers.abstract: Holographic tensor networks are a central route to understanding the mechanism behind the holographic duality, but standard fixed-graph constructions with maximally entangled links face a structural obstacle. Their leading entanglement spectra are flat, so their R\'enyi entropies do not depend on the replica index. This is in sharp contrast with holographic conformal field theories, where a tensionful cosmic brane makes the refined R\'enyi entropy $n$-dependent. Capturing this replica dependence is therefore an important test of tensor-network descriptions of holographic entanglement. We construct an explicit family of replica-dependent geodesic graphs that reproduces this behavior while keeping the links maximally entangled. For each replica index $n$, geodesics are emitted from the replicated boundary with the same local, isotropic intersection measure. They perfectly tessellate the selected replica geometry, so the $n$-dependence of their intersection counts comes from the geometry. Tensor-network models on these graphs reproduce the cosmic-brane prescription for refined R\'enyi entropy by counting crossing threads. Their cross-copy endpoint density also agrees, in CFT$_2$, with a boundary reconstruction within the additive linear combination proposal, providing a check beyond the total entropy. In higher dimensions, we further obtain an analytic large-separation decay law for this density.

papers.title: Quantum black hole evaporation from thin shell collapse: a complete effective picture
papers.abstract: Quantum gravity is expected to play a central role in resolving classical singularities and providing a complete, predictive spacetime picture. In this paper, we develop an effective model inspired by loop quantum gravity that aims to fulfill this expectation, providing a unified description of thin shell collapse, black hole formation, evaporation, and remnant dynamics. The framework exhibits general validity, holding across different effective equations of motion, matter sources, and evaporation laws. Specifically, we incorporate backreaction within a quasi-static approximation, modeling the radiation as null dust and matching the ingoing and outgoing fluxes across an evaporation surface using the Darmois-Israel junction conditions. For an evaporation law governed by the Stefan-Boltzmann law, we find that the final stage of evaporation yields an extremal black hole extending into a new asymptotic region, featuring both event and Cauchy horizons. Conversely, under the Schwinger approach, no event or Cauchy horizons form, instead, a temporary dynamical trapped region emerges, and the resulting spacetime remains globally hyperbolic. Under this variant, our model predicts a horizonless null remnant escaping to future null infinity.

papers.title: Split Ends: UV Physics branches Black Hole Hair
papers.abstract: Coupling a shift-symmetric scalar field to the Gauss-Bonnet invariant modifies black holes (BHs) via scalar hair. Here we consider this field to be the Goldstone of a complex scalar field with a symmetry-breaking potential. For BHs of a size comparable with the inverse mass gap, the gapped field tries to restore the symmetry close to the horizon, enhancing the departure from standard BHs. Moreover, BHs of the same mass can have up to three different horizon areas and surface gravities. This branching has profound consequences for BH physics, potentially observable in gravitational waves.

papers.title: The Relaxation of Quantum Near-Extremal Black Holes. (I) Microcanonical States, Pruning of Quasinormal Modes, and the Aretakis Instability
papers.abstract: The late-time relaxation of a near-extremal black hole is classically governed by an infinite tower of purely damped quasinormal modes. This poses a puzzle: the higher overtones decay at rates much larger than the energy $E$ of the black hole above extremality, so they would need black hole states below the extremal mass. We resolve it by including the quantum fluctuations that become large when $E$ falls below a scale $E_b$. We compute the retarded Green's function of a probe of conformal dimension $\Delta$ in a black hole of fixed energy, and find that each classical mode splits into a pair of poles with real parts set by $E_b$. The perturbed black hole decays as an unstable quantum system, and a pair is a resonance, i.e., a quasinormal mode, only if its energy lies within the accessible black hole spectrum. This prunes the tower to finitely many modes, all damped faster than $\Delta^2E_b$, and below $E=\Delta^2E_b/2$ none is left. For generic $\Delta$, the response of the black hole decays first as $t^{-2\Delta}$ and finally as $t^{-3/2}$, with an exponential stage in between if $E\gg\Delta^2E_b$. The same quantum effects bear on the Aretakis instability of extremal black holes, in which transverse derivatives of a perturbation grow without bound on the horizon. Like the tower of modes, it originates in the scale invariance of the classical throat, which the quantum fluctuations break. The $t^{-2\Delta}$ decay, which is the boundary counterpart of the Aretakis growth, ends by $t\sim1/E_b$, when the throat ceases to be classical, and by then horizon derivatives have grown only to a finite value. Their unbounded growth is an artifact of taking the semiclassical limit before the late-time one, two limits that in quantum mechanics do not commute.
